700818.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew אָמֵן (āmḗn, “so be it”, “surely”).

700802.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂mélǵti, from *h₂melǵ- (“to milk”). Cognates include Latin mulgeō, Old English meolc (English milk), Gothic 𐌼𐌹𐌻𐌿𐌺𐍃 (miluks), and Albanian mjel.

700855.t: From Proto-Hellenic *abnós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂egʷnós. Cognates include Latin agnus, Old Church Slavonic агнѧ (agnę), Old English ēanian (English yean), and Albanian enjë.

700880.t: Perhaps from an earlier *ἀμυ-νϝ-ω (*amu-nw-ō), a thematicized nasal present verbal formation (a la κλίνω (klínō) and πλύνω (plúnō)) from a root ἀμυ- (amu-) which may also be found in ἀμεύομαι (ameúomai, “to surpass, outstrip”), though the semantics are…

700854.t: From ἄμνηστος (ắmnēstos, “forgotten, forgetful”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun suffix), ultimately from μνάομαι (mnáomai, “remember”).

700821.t: From ἀ- (a-, privative alpha) + μιαίνω (miaínō, “stain, defile”) + -τος (-tos).

700845.t: Traditionally considered a contamination of ἄμαθος (ắmăthos, “sand”) and ψάμμος (psắmmos, “sand”).

700870.t: Difficult to explain as an inherited Indo-European word and usually considered to be a Pre-Greek/substrate word. Compare also Proto-Indo-European *h₂ébōl (“apple”).

700851.t: As if from *ἄμνητος (ámnētos) ("forgetful") + -ία (-íā), from ἀ- (a-) + μιμνήσκω (mimnḗskō) + -τος (-tos).

700883.t: ἀμφι- (amphi-, “amphi-, on two sides”) + βάλλω (bállō, “to throw”).

700819.t: From ἀμάω (amáō, “to harvest, gather”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂meh₁- (“to reap, mow, harvest”) (whence also English mow, meadow).

700890.t: From ἀμφι- (ămphĭ-, “on both sides”) + ὁδός (hodós, “way; path”).
